entry.title: [BIP Draft] Co-signer Spending Policies
entry.summary:
A robust open lending protocol designed to replace traditional rehypothecating lenders incorporates a set of foundational principles that ensure transparency, security, and user autonomy. Unlike collapsed platforms such as Celsius and BlockFi—which pooled customer assets, held custody over them, and re-lent funds—this model mandates that each loan is managed individually on a one-to-one basis. At no point does the protocol take custody of collateral or reuse it for other loans, significantly reducing systemic risks and mismanagement.
Borrowers retain full control over their assets by holding their own keys, utilizing industry standards like Partially Signed Bitcoin Transactions (PSBTs) and descriptors. This guarantees that they can always recover their collateral independently without relying on a third party. The system features an open offer board, such as listings on platforms like Nostr, where loan offers are transparently posted, and private negotiations can occur between interested parties.
Ensuring fair risk management, price feeds are sourced from signed data provided by established Discreet Log Contract (DLC) oracles. These feeds monitor the loan-to-value ratio in real time and serve as triggers for automated liquidations if collateral value falls below agreed thresholds. Additionally, the role of a payment attestor is crucial; this entity provides cryptographically signed proofs confirming that repayments have occurred, whether through the Lightning Network or directly on-chain.
Collateral release or liquidation is strictly governed by a co-signer, who acts according to pre-agreed policies and never unilaterally controls the funds. This role is standardized by BIP specifications, ensuring consistent and reliable enforcement across implementations. To enhance both borrower and lender security, an alert service notifies parties of margin calls or approaching deadlines but lacks the authority to move any funds, thus preserving asset safety.
Finally, all loan agreements are structured using templates that are easily interpretable by both humans and software. Each agreement is tied to a specific policy ID, promoting clarity and enforceability. Overall, this architecture provides a transparent, decentralized alternative to legacy custodial lending models, eliminating many of the risks associated with asset pooling and rehypothecation.
